note: IDENTITY AND PROFILE METADATA ONLY. This file deliberately does NOT list which Node versions are supported — that list lives in docs/compat/node-v4.json and is sliced by position at min_supported, so there is exactly one place to move a floor. This file supplies what that list cannot: which commit each tag pointed at when it was first resolved, and what a case against it claims. A version the manifest supports but this file does not pin fails the plan rather than being tested against whatever the tag points at today.

contract_source.note: THE SOURCE THE PINNED-SOURCE CONTRACT JOB TESTS, named here rather than taken from PSP's go.mod. When the job resolved it from go.mod, the evidence for 'PSP speaks to a real released Node' moved whenever a dependency bump happened, and removing the PN root dependency (X07) would have removed the test entry point with it. A commit, not a tag: the matrix resolves the commit and checks it, so a moved tag is caught instead of silently testing a different revision.

pinned_sources_note: THESE ARE COMMITS, NOT TAG OBJECTS. `git ls-remote --tags` lists both refs/tags/X (the annotated tag object) and refs/tags/X^{} (the commit it points at); pinning the former fails every leg, because a checkout resolves to the commit. The matrix verifies the resolved commit against these, so a wrong-but-well-formed SHA is caught on the first run rather than after it has quietly tested a different revision.
